checks.claim: Request is canonical native JSON bytes, independently loaded and evaluated by each side. Neither side receives the other decoded object or result.

Exact seven envelope fields and fixed schema/correlation/status/diagnostic/flag/tag checks precede comparison. Canonical output rejects floats and nonnative trees, preserves native bool versus int and array order, sorts object keys only, removes no value fields.

Full canonical response bytes are compared. First-difference lookup traverses dict fields and ordered array elements only to diagnose an already failed complete comparison; it is not the equality algorithm.

Both actual statuses must equal each concrete generator declaration. Valid versus negative consistency is checked first, so equal blanket rejection cannot pass valid cases. Actual side counters are incremented from validated returned statuses and separately reported on success.

Exactly1024 ordered native integer seeds and unique schema3 case IDs are required; all10 operation names and512/512 input partitions are asserted. Premature next failure is technical with seed; an extra element or exhaustion error prevents successful completion.
Canonical decoded inputs must equal original request bytes before evaluation and their own original decoded bytes afterward. No returned response equality can override an input mutation failure.

Loader/evaluator/serialization exceptions become DifferentialTechnicalFailure with chained cause and seed/case context; no exception is normalized into a business response. Declared-status, stream and structural failures also stop the gate.

Complete-success summary lies after stream exhaustion and all final count/coverage assertions. It reports actual classifications and length-framed request/reference/target SHA256 streams; source makes no runtime/capacity/D2 claim.

Five definitions include typed/order/extra-field, unknown-exception, reject-all and premature-exhaustion negative controls. Source contains no financial formula, expected money constant or DTO builder.
